[b]World News[/b]

[b]Belorev filled sails[/b]

The Department of National Defence today announced at 10:00 am that Irving Shipbuilding Inc. and the Republic of Ostarev came to an agreement in regards to the [i]Sapummijjuti[/i] class coastal corvette. Irving has agreed to the sale of six new [i]Sapummijjuti[/i] corvettes at BC$73.88 million ($54.16 million) per unit, bringing the total to BC$443.36 million ($325 million). It is the first international purchase of the [i]Sapummijjuti[/i] class.

The deal comes as part of the Republic of Ostarev's policy of both expanding and upgrading its armed forces as tensions in the Belorev region continue to increase following the recent terror attack on the Grand Jazeran Hotel in Rustavi, Qarestan yesterday morning at 8:00 am. The purchase is also a trend in Bascover's own foreign policy as it continues to increase its presence in the region via trade.

[b]Aurora reaches out[/b]

Following a press conference outside the headquarters of Aurora Airlines in Fairfield, Mary, Chairman Vagn Sørensen revealed that He and the Board permitted President and CEO, Michael Rousseau, to reach out to Chairman Herod Gaines and CEO Vanessa Adler of Air New Westmore in the hopes of establishing a airline alliance that would cement the two airlines as the powerhouses of international travel.

The proposed alliance, which Mr. Rousseau has dupped the [i]SkyTeam[/i], would involve a two-tier rewards program with incentives including priority boarding and upgrades, inter-airline codeshare connections within countries to allow for cost reductions in operation facilities, staff, investments and purchases. With Aurora Airlines already operating out of three international airports in New Westmore, Mr. Rousseau believes that the transition is [b]"inevitable"[/b] and will [b]"[...]be without problems [or] interruptions[...]"[/b]. 

It's understood that should [i]SkyTeam[/i] take off, Mr. Rousseau is keen for further partnership with other international airlines.

[b]Destination of choice: Western Shamat[/b]

Western Shamat has been the latest hotspot for Bascoveran companies, with a number of them establishing themselves in countries along the east coast. Recently, the Erene Sports Programming Network (ESPN) establish a new Iroccan subdivision based in the capital of the Sealiphate, Imdekka. The subdivision, known as Irocco-Erene Sports Programming Network (Irocco-SPN), was created following the signing of a deal of undisclosed worth that would require ESPN to found a separate division that was partially owned by the Iroccan Government. The reasoning for this was due to Iroccan laws regarding the practice and advertisement of gambling within its programs. Irocco-SPN removes all advertising of gambling in games and during commercial breaks in stoppage time. Currently, Irocco-SPN shows live games of the Iroccan domestic T20 cricket league, as well as replays of all Bascoveran sports games, such as the Major Hockey League and the ARC Energy Professional Football League Men. Live games are unavailable due to several teams across both leagues having sponsorship deals with gambling business, and as such are digitally removed by a team of editors to allow the showing of replays.

Aurora Airlines continued to make the news when it also announced that starting April this year, it would be operating out of both Irocco and the Gold Kingdom of Dhornaper. While it's been released that Aurora will fly in and out of airports in Imdekka and Ryhdi in Irocco, nothing of yet has been said in regards to the airports which Aurora will operate in in Dhornaper. Imdekka airport in Irocco is officially the most northern hub of Aurora Airlines.

Yet another Bascoveran company has established itself on the east coast, once more in Irocco and Dhornaper. The company in question is Dunkin' Donuts, a popular fast food restaurant that offers a variety of options such as coffee and donuts. Dunkin' owners, Dunkin' Brands Group, Inc., who also own Baskin-Robbins, came to a agreement with both respective governments to open several restaurants across both nations while conforming to Halal practices and religious customs of the nations. Dunkin' Brands Group, Inc. has also stated it will source its ingredients from local farmers and hire from within the communities they are based.

[b]Defence News[/b]

[b]New roommate and new toys[/b]

Chief of the Bascoveran Navy, Rear Admiral Oliver Berdal has confirmed with reporters that the Department of National Defence has finalised a deal with the United States of Lockheed in regards to the purchase of a Type 076 drone carrier-amphibious assault ship (also classed as a Landing Helicopter Dock). The deal, worth BC$4.09 billion ($3 billion), will see the immediate transfer of a domestically commissioned Type 076 vessel to the Bascoveran Navy where it will be confiruged with a new compliment of fighter jets, helicopters, and drones to effectively carry out the defence of Bascover's waters. As the original $3 billion cost would take up 37% of the $7.981 billion (BC$10.81 billion) national defence budget, another agreement was made with the USL.

The Parliament of Bascover has granted the Armed Forces of Lockheed the lease of both a air base and a naval base within Bascover to carry out missions in tandem with the Bascoveran Armed Forces. In exchange, the USL has agreed to cover 70% of the $3 billion deal, thus leaving Bascover with only having to pay $BC1.23 billion ($900 million), a massive relief.

The air base is based in Kumuk on Bascover island, while the naval base will be to its far east in Canopus, the capital of the island Carina.

[b]Sports News[/b]

[b]Jets soar to the Crown[/b]

The Duncan Jets have been crowned as the regular season champions of the Major Hockey League (MHL) following their 2 - 3 shootout victory against third placed Sinunimak Krakens at Climate Pledge Arena, Sinunimak. Even though there is still one round left till the end of the regular season and beginning of the playoffs, it is now mathematically impossible for second placed team with 12 points, Parksville Penguins, to overtake the Duncan Jets who sit at 17 points. The Jets have now won five games in a row.

The second placed Parksville Penguins host the Duncan Jets and will need a win to guarantee their place in the playoffs. Third placed Sinunimak Krakens currently have 10 points, and will need to defeat fifth placed Campbell River Flames to gain the needed 2 points to tie with the Krakens. However, the Krakens will be hoping for the Penguins to suffer a blowout against the Jets, as the current point differential favours the Jets who have +10 (30 GF, 20 GA)  while the Krakens are on -1 (23 GF, 24 GA). The Penguins are currently the highest rated offensive team in the MHL, and pundits doubt the Krakens chances of getting the necessary scores.

[b]Eastern Expansion Evolution[/b]

Discussions between the Major Hockey League Board of Governors, MHL Commissioner Herbet Rilley, and the Hockey Associations of the islands of Halifax, Utah, and Carina have finally come to an end after almost a year of negotiations. Originally, it was planned for the three associations to join the MHL as part of its eastern expansion as a singular team known as [b]"Eastern United"[/b], however, the long standing personal feud between Halifax Hockey Association President and former Campbell River Flames goaltender Henry Lund, and Utah Hockey Association President and former Mary Sabers left winger and captain Alexander Pickett has been a constant road block in the negotiations.

Their feud, which carried on from 2000 till both of their retirement in 2020, has caused a number of delays in the expansion which was planned to take effect at the start of the 202627 season, with many fearing that the expansion wouldn't take fruition at all. Thankfully however, the MHL, Lund, and Pickett were able to come to a new agreement to allow for the eastern expansion for the 202829 season.

Both the Halifax Hockey Association and the Carina Hockey Association will join the MHL as the 11[sup]th[/sup] joint venture under the name of the Eastern Maple Leafs and will play their home games at Capbank Arena in Canopus, Carina and at Irving Centre in Torbay, Halifax. They will be the first team to have two home arenas and the first to represent two islands. The Utah Hockey Association will still join the MHL, but will do so as their own independent team under the Utah Mammoths, making them officially the 12[sup]th[/sup] team to join the MHL. Pickett posted on social media that the Mammoths home games would be played at Delta Centre in Honeywhale City, Utah. 

Fans online have already beginning to cultivate this newly established rivalry, with many calling it the Battle of the Straits.

[spoiler= Wellassonan Premier League reaches halfway point] 
[i]Wellassonan National News - Новеллсти Нациоьнлыы Веласоньый. Sunday, 23 January 2028[/i]

The 110th season of the Wellassonan Premier League, the highest level of Association football in the country, is now halfway completed. The season has been a highly competitive one, akin to last season, albeit with distinct differences.

In the previous season, Spartak Otvragivod were crowned champions, winning their 23rd title. They racked up an impressive 86 points, narrowly beating out 2nd place Zefhir Sankt-Elenaston by two points. This was notable because, at the halfway point, Zefhir were ahead of Spartak by 5 points, with Spartak's 1st place finished considered an upset.

Few people expected CSKA Otvragivod to be a serious title contender this year. They finished 5th in the previous season, and were not expected to significantly improve in the subsequent season. Nevertheless, despite low expectations, they currently stand at top of the table with 43 points, 2 points ahead of Spartak. CSKA have 13 wins, 4 draws, and 2 losses, while Spartak has 12 wins, 5 draws, and 2 losses. Analysts expect the title race to be close, but still predict Spartak to win their 24th title, which will be their 3rd consecutive title if achieved.

Meanwhile, Zefhir Sankt-Elenaston has had a poorer season this year. Despite high promises as likely title contenders, they currently have 12 wins, 1 draw, and 6 losses, being 6 points behind CSKA. Whille not out of the realm of possibilities, it is considered increasingly unlikely that Zefhir will win the title if their current form continues.

Faktchel Yandsleyovsk, Al-Pudar, FK Elena, VMSK Otvragivod, and Dynamo Otvragivod round out the top 8, each having consistent, albeit rather unsurprising seasons. With 19 games still to play, anything can happen in the Wellassonan Premier League!
[/spoiler]
